title: SHAPEN IN INIQUITY: RESETTING THE NERVOUS SYSTEM

sense.text:
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” The Lord made man from the dust of the ground. Man did not come from primates and evolve over time into what we know today as human beings. That is not true. The Bible says man was made from the dust of the ground.

Science is only good if it goes with the Bible. If it contradicts the Bible, we don’t give a damn about science; we only look for the science that agrees with what the Bible says. And the logical ones know it: the human body is made of the same elements found in the soil. Oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, calcium and phosphorus make up over 99% of our mass. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are found in every cell, and the same things are in the soil. The essential minerals are there too: calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium for enzymes and energy, sodium and chlorine for fluid balance. The trace elements as well: iron for carrying oxygen in the blood, which is why the doctor says your iron is low; zinc for immune function and wound healing, which is why they told everyone to take zinc during COVID; silicon for connective tissue, skin and bone; manganese for enzymes. Soil is the building blocks, and the Lord built Adam from the dust of the ground.

So the scientists who come out of nowhere saying we evolved from primates do it to contradict God’s word, because God is a black man and they hate black people. But every human being walking this earth is a testament that God’s word is true, and we just so happen to be the best, because we have the melanin. We are the sons of God, descended directly from Adam’s lineage. We come from the earth and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says. The most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things; he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground.

The other nations make sure we are deficient in these things. Much of the food we eat and what we put into our bodies diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important to keep a healthy diet, especially for the brothers trying to get themselves in shape.

precepts.why: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth”. All men are from the ground. Everything done in Israel United in Christ is to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. So when someone asks how we know man was made from the dust of the ground, when the white man’s science says otherwise, the Bible answers: Adam was created of earth.

“The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The first man, Adam, is of the earth; the second man is Christ.

“As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy”. As Adam was earthy, so are we. We all come from the same soil our father Adam came from. “And as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly”: that goes to the celestial body.

“And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” We have borne the image of the earthy, meaning we are mortal: Adam lost his immortality. But the rest of the verse is a promise from God. We were born in this flesh from the soil, but the Lord is going to make us again. He is going to change our cellular structure and give us a new body, no longer this weak, frail body that has to die. Our soul has to come up out of this body and the Lord has to give us a new one. Tired of the back hurting, tired of waking up with a belly ache: that is what we are waiting for.

sense.text: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” Adam was made from the dust of the ground, but the Lord gave him immortality. In the beginning he could not die.

“Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.” They that hold on Satan’s side, following Satan, his doctrine and his idolatry, are going to die with him.

The only way back to the immortality is to come back to the Lord. That is it. The only way to get back to what we were naturally supposed to be is to return to your God. No idol can give you eternal life, because they are not gods: no Buddha, Krishna, Vishnu, Allah, none of the Egyptology, Set or Ra, all that crap. Nobody gives eternal life but the man that orchestrated it, the most High God of Israel. Going off into these other doctrines because you are feeling some type of way is missing out on eternal life. Eternal life comes through one source: the Most High.

precepts.why:
Christ said it: “For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.” To quicken is to make the dead alive. Christ has the same power.

And here is a jab at the trinitarians: “For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. For me to commit something to you, I had to have it first and you didn’t. If I give you this phone, you did not have a phone before I gave it to you. That means I am superior to you and have authority over you; I gave you something you did not have, because I created you. The Father committed judgment to Christ.

Why? “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” The Father has the supreme honour, and gives the Son something so that people will honour him as they honour the Father. That means the Father is over him. Co-eternal, co-substantial: stop arguing with these people. “He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him.”

“He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.” The only way to get life is to believe on Christ and keep the commandments. That is the only way to eternal life, the immortality that Adam had at the beginning and lost through sin.

sense.text: “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” Adam bore a wicked heart, transgressed and was overcome. Since Adam sinned, everybody that comes after him, which is all of us, the earthy that have borne his image, have sinned as well.

“Thus infirmity was made permanent”. An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness, frailty or ailment, often tied to old age, chronic illness or disability; a lack of strength that reduces a person’s vitality. Adam was not feeling physical pain when he was first created. When he got cast down, now his joints hurt, his back, his fingers from digging in the dirt, planting crops and building houses. Adam had everything. When he got cast down, everybody got cast down with him, and now we feel backaches, bodyaches and headaches. The woman has her menstrual cycle and feels the cramps; she feels the pain when the baby is in her belly. Why? Because of Adam’s sin. When our father fell, we all fell with him, and now we all face infirmity, physical and mental weakness. The mental is the focus: our bodies are now susceptible to ailments, frailty, sickness and mental weakness because of the sin of our father, and we have continued in those sins.

“So that the good departed away”: that immortality, that understanding of God’s word. God gave Adam the word in the beginning. That is how his wife knew God said they should not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil: her husband taught her. The Lord taught Adam the commandments. “And the evil abode still”: we still have that evil nature, and it is in our flesh.

“And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done: for they also had a wicked heart”. This is the foundation before going deep into the mind and the nervous system: when our forefather Adam sinned, we all fell with him. We lost immortality, and now we have these frail physical and mental weaknesses and ailments because of it.

precepts.why:
“For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness hath it brought up unto this time?” Adam’s first sin and that evil heart he had, how much more ungodliness has it brought up unto this time?

“And how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?” The time of threshing is when Christ returns. Until Christ comes we are going to be surrounded by evil; there will always be evil in society. It is inevitable. That is why Bishop Yawasap and the elders say we are not trying to build a metropolis, but a nation within a nation. That is why we gather together and have different offices in the body to benefit our people. Christ is the one who is going to correct all this wickedness, give us immortality and change our vile body to be fashioned as his glorious body. But while we are here we have a job to do: to heal ourselves so that we can heal our people. Get yourself together so you can benefit your people.

“Ponder now by thyself, how great fruit of wickedness the grain of evil seed hath brought forth.” Look at how much wickedness that grain of evil seed has brought forth.

“O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Ezra is saying: Adam, what have you done? Not only did you fall, we all fell with you.

Our forefathers had enough understanding to know why we are in the condition we are in. And we furthered our own affliction by sinning against the most High God. We made it worse, and we keep making it worse as a race, as a nation of people.

sense.text:
“Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.” An officer, Elisha in San Antonio, was teaching on a college campus when an Edomite pastor rolled up on him with a film crew talking about the virgin birth, and this scripture came up. The officer asked him: did Christ sin? He was stuck. No, he did not. But he was shapen in iniquity too, in this same flesh. So what does it mean? Though Christ was in this sinful flesh, he did not give in to it, which means we can do it too. He is a merciful and faithful high priest who set an example that we should follow his steps.

So when the Bible says “Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me”, it is talking about the sinful nature of this flesh: a nature you do not have to give in to, though people give in to it day to day. We can overcome the things in our mind, the things we have been through, our trauma. But it is up to us to have our mind right with the Lord to do so. That is where the power lies.

Stop letting these people convince you that you don’t have to keep God’s commandments. When people go back to their old environment, it is trauma they are going back to. They feel comfortable in that traumatic state, comfortable in who they used to be. They have low self-esteem, they don’t believe the scriptures, they don’t have faith, so they go right back to the vomit, because it is more comfortable to sit in your crap than to stand up as a man and change your mind. That is why some people stay overweight: they have not conditioned their mind that I’m a man of God and I’m going to do something about this weight. A man who says he is defeated is giving in to trauma. We have the word of God. We have the keys to break all that. No excuses.

precepts.why: “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” That is the sinful nature of the flesh. Christ did not give anyone a license to sin here. He told them: watch and pray, because I know your spirit wants to do right, but don’t sleep on that flesh you are in. Adam fell, and I know what flesh you are in; I know you are tempted. Don’t fall into the temptation. He gave them the keys.

“For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” Why is Paul carnal? Because he is in this carnal flesh. “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” He is talking about the mental anguish he battles. He knows he is supposed to think sober thoughts, yet at times Satan creeps into his thoughts. I don’t want these thoughts; I want to keep God’s laws. Paul is not admitting to being in any sin. He is telling you that mentally he is fighting against the flesh.

“If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” When you think about watching porn and then remember the commandment and say I can’t watch porn, you consent that the law is good. When you could lie and don’t, because the Bible says lie not one to another, you just consented that God’s law is good. Sister, when the thought comes up to gainsay your lord and you catch yourself, you just said God’s law is stronger than your flesh. Every time we choose God’s word over sin, we say God is right and I am wrong. So when somebody tells you that you can’t keep God’s laws, that is a damn lie. They don’t get up and murder people or rob banks, because they consent that the law is good. Although we are in this carnal flesh, we prove every day that we can apply God’s commandments to our life. The Christians can’t do this; they are not equipped for it. They are excuse makers, undisciplined and weak.

“Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.” When these thoughts come, it is no longer me, because I want to do right; it is sin still in me. “For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing”. There is no good thing in this flesh, because Adam sinned, we got cast down, and we all furthered that sin. Over time we gained trauma, depression, all kinds of anxieties and mental illnesses, ailments, frailties and infirmities, because we continue in sin. The Lord keeps allowing it: you keep adding sin to sin, so you stay in this condition.

“For to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.” I want to do right, but how do I get out of this flesh? I don’t know. “Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.” That is why Deacon Malachi does not look at a brother as evil the moment he makes a mistake. Everybody does something for a reason, and you have to ask why. We know you committed the sin, but what does it stem from? The only way to healing is to know where it stems from.

“I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me.” When Paul wants his mind right according to the commandments, sin is always hovering over him, the old man always trying to pull him back into wickedness. “For I delight in the law of God after the inward man”: that is what Christ said, the spirit is willing. “But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.” This body don’t play fair. That is why Christ said don’t sleep on that flesh; it is something you can fall to if you are not right in the spirit.

“O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?” When I look at myself in this flesh, I am wretched. “I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.” With the mind I serve the law of God, but in this flesh I catch myself falling into the sinful nature again. This is the battle of every man and woman on this earth. The difference between them and us is that we know why we battle it, and we have the keys to fix it.

sense.text: “For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain.” Because of the things we have been through, some of us do things and don’t even know why. Some of us have anger issues and don’t know where they stem from; we just know we are always mad. Some are depressed and cannot find the source; some feel numb; some have a heart rate that is always up. Some people are always sweating, and sweat shows the heart rate has gone up. If it is not hot and you are sitting in the air conditioning, something is turning your wheel: some mental anguish is working inside and putting you in a flurry. Our devices are but uncertain.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” This is the earthy tabernacle, as it said: as is the earthy, such are they that are earthy, all that come of Adam.

In the Bible, to muse is to think deeply, meditate, ponder or murmur on something, especially God’s word or works: to consider closely, to study in silence. When the Bible says our mind muses on many things, that is us: why did that person die, why is my life like this, where did I go wrong, should I have married her, should I have gone to that job interview, why did I get drunk last night? Most of you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the man up thinking about what could happen to his daughters. This earthy tabernacle is what causes us to overthink and overanalyse everything.

precepts.why: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used: I muse. He would think about why life was the way it is, why we suffer certain conditions; deep, quiet contemplation of God’s works, acts and commandments. Muse and meditate are used interchangeably. Ezra did the same: it was not his mind to know the deep things, he only wanted to know why Israel was suffering what it was going through.

sense.text:
“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements”. This is Solomon, saying the Lord gave him knowledge.

Everything in the class builds to this: we came from the earth, we are corruptible, our father broke God’s commandments and his infirmity has been passed down to us, and now we are fighting to get back to immortality. In that fight we have to identify the things within ourselves that make us the way we are, heal from them and move on. Many of us act the way we do because of traumatic experiences we went through. That is not the end for us. This is why God brought this truth back to us in these last days: he is giving us the keys to the kingdom of heaven. It is up to us to put the key in the ignition and crank the car.

“The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts”: that is what they now call zoology. “The violence of winds”: meteorology. “And the reasonings of men”: psychology. Solomon was not just a king; Solomon was a psychologist, and so was his father David. What Solomon wrote in Proverbs he learned from his father; read Psalms and you will see it repeated. Abraham was a psychologist. Noah and Moses too. We picture them as old white men in the desert. No. These are the men of the most High God, the sons of God.

precepts.why:
“This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him”. Some of us fall asleep reading the Bible, then go to YouTube and watch TED talks on psychology, not knowing that all of their research comes from one foundational piece: the Bible.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the way of knowledge: psychology, neurology, how the brain works. Our forefathers knew how to heal people of their infirmities. Before there was surgery, God gave our forefathers power to lay hands on a brother and he came back. Christ touched people and their bones snapped back in place; that is surgery, but it came from spiritual power. The white man has been trying to copy what happens in this Bible. At the United Nations they give everyone an earpiece to hear in their own language; that happened at Pentecost. In Genesis 11 everyone spoke one language and the Lord confounded it; now they learn many languages in school. He is always trying to play God. So read your Bible again with new eyes, not from a place of boredom and not from the white man’s perspective.

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” The most High never came down on earth. So who is this God who gave us this wisdom? The Son of God, Jesus the Christ. He came down and taught us the wisdom, and gave the apostles power for a moment to do what he could do. Brothers and sisters, learn this Bible again.

sense.text: “Great travail is created for every man, and an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam”. Because of Adam’s sins we all carry that heavy yoke, “from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, till the day that they return to the mother of all things”: from the day you are born to the day you die. This is what man goes through.
“Their imagination of things to come, and the day of death, trouble their thoughts, and cause fear of heart”. Your mind is troubled; you fear death, and you have fear of heart.

“From him that sitteth on a throne of glory, unto him that is humbled in earth and ashes”. It does not matter if you are rich or if you are poor: every man and woman has the same issues. Money does not heal trauma. That is why so many athletes and entertainers lose their minds when they retire, when they get old, when they are away from the drugs and alcohol. When they have to actually be themselves, they go crazy.

“Wrath, and envy, trouble, and unquietness, fear of death, and anger, and strife, and in the time of rest upon his bed his night sleep, do change his knowledge.” You overthink at night when you are sleeping. Some wake up out of dreams: evil dreams, dreams of death, of losing a loved one, of losing a job, even dreams of committing adultery, and you wake up and thank God you didn’t do it, and say, Lord, take this from me. Why am I having that dream?

“A little or nothing is his rest”: you can’t sleep. “And afterward he is in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, troubled in the vision of his heart, as if he were escaped out of a battle.” You are troubled by the dream you just had, and you wake up as if you escaped out of a battle. “When all is safe, he awaketh, and marvelleth that the fear was nothing.” Thank God it was just a dream. All of us have gone through it, every man and woman, because Adam fell and we have all fallen.

“Such things happen unto all flesh, both man and beast”. You have seen a dog jump out of its dream. Even the beast goes through it. “And that is sevenfold more upon sinners”: it is seven times worse if you are in sin.

Here is what that means in the body. The nervous system has the central nervous system, the brain and spinal cord, the command centre, and the peripheral nervous system, the nerves that run to every part of the body. Put your hand on a hot stove and the brain sends the signal to pull the finger away and feel the pain. The nervous system is built to protect you. But it can be used for good or for evil; that is why Paul said, when I would do good, evil is present with me. The autonomic system runs what you don’t think about: breathing, heart rate, digestion. The sympathetic side is fight or flight: someone rolls up on you and you put your hands up or you run. The parasympathetic side is rest and digest: calm, conserving energy and healing. For many of us that part is broken. We can’t get calm, barely sleep, don’t heal, and some have bodies that attack themselves.

Under stress and trauma the amygdala, the threat detector, fires all the time: don’t trust my wife, my children, my co-workers, nobody. So you stay to yourself, smoke your weed, play video games, and don’t bother anybody until you want sex or food. Many of us lived that life. Under extreme trauma the body can freeze, going numb and dissociated, or fawn: you put yourself to work because you can never calm down, cleaning and moving all the time. Trauma changes the brain: the amygdala, the hippocampus that holds memory and context, and the prefrontal cortex that makes decisions. That is why some keep making horrible decisions and can’t understand why; why some are always on edge, irritable, anxious, panicky; why some are numb, exhausted and disconnected, missing assignments, late, absent from the Telegram. The first thing we say is he is out of the spirit, he has the devil on him; that may be true, but we should ask why. Sisters with postpartum depression know that numbness: the baby is crying and you don’t hear it.

The vagus nerve brings the body back to calm, and under prolonged trauma it becomes less efficient, which leads to prolonged anxiety and depression. Your depression is rooted in your body, in what you put into it, and in sin. That is why it is sevenfold more upon sinners. But there is hope, and the word of God is how we get over it. Ongoing traumatic stress brings high blood pressure, digestive problems, chronic pain and weak immunity. Sisters are hormonal, the weaker vessel, and a sister must reset her nervous system by getting her mind right according to God’s word to have the motivation to push through the numbness into the gym. That is where husbands and leaders come in: we set the example. There should be no fat men among us. The men lead the nation; nobody is coming to lead it for us. We are the firstfruits of Christ and we must set the nation in order.

The adverse childhood experiences study found that abuse, neglect, a parent with mental illness or addiction, incarceration, divorce and domestic violence in childhood bring sickness later in life, and that 67% of people had at least one. Go back to this verse: “Such things happen unto all flesh”, as the study found; “and that is sevenfold more upon sinners.” The men of the Bible were psychologists and doctors. And who did they teach to sin? What community do they keep in sin, knowing it leads to sickness later? The liquor store, the drug dealing, the Arab stores in our community; no banks, no businesses, no loans. It is systematic: the medical field, law enforcement, the courts, the government, the funeral home and the pharmaceutical companies all make money off us and what we have been through. That is why you brothers are called to heal. Millions of our people are waiting on us to teach them the word of God and help them heal, and to tell them there is a God coming to save them.

“And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.” Martha had a sister called Mary; they invited Christ into their house, and Mary decided to sit and hear Christ’s words.

“But Martha was cumbered about much serving”. Cumbered about much serving: she was in a fawn response, moving around, I have to do this, I have to take care of that, unable to calm down. Some develop things like OCD this way: I have to clean, I have to move. Sit down and get some rest? I can’t. “Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.”

“Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.” Christ said: Mary decided to sit down and hear the word of God, but you are moving all over the place. Sit down somewhere and listen to these words. Like Martha, some of us immerse ourselves in things to do so we don’t have to deal with our thoughts. There is nothing wrong with labour, because the Bible also says be not idle; we have to find a balance. Sometimes you have to sit down and let your brain and body rest, meditate in the word of God, fast, pray. You can’t always be up moving around.

“Let this be the reward of mine adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. But do thou for me, O God the Lord, for thy name’s sake: because thy mercy is good, deliver thou me.” Your mercy is good, Lord. Deliver me. From what?

“For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.” David was experiencing trauma. The word trauma, from the 1690s, comes from the Greek for a wound, a hurt, a defeat; to be traumatized is to be wounded, an emotional scar. A wound has to be treated so that it can be healed.

These men were psychologists; they understood emotions. Women say on podcasts that men are not emotionally intelligent and don’t understand emotional regulation. Our forefathers taught us all that. King David said, my heart is wounded: that is trauma.

precepts.why: “A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.” The spirit is broken: that is trauma. This book is not only for the prophecies, the dietary laws and how to break down Jews and Gentiles. The Bible is also a tool, a weapon, a medicine cabinet for us to heal ourselves. But you have to believe that.

“The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart”: a broken heart is trauma. “And saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.” How is the Lord near you? Through the Bible. You have the words to break it all. They did not count on us picking up this book and learning the truth about who we are: that we are above all nations, how to change our diet, how to control our sexual desires and concupiscence, how to stop lying, how to set up order and structure in our communities. There is a God, and there is the Holy Spirit, the comforter the Lord sent to comfort us in our trauma. But you have to believe you can heal from it.

sense.text:
“For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” This is how they keep the system going. The study’s pyramid starts with adverse childhood experiences at the bottom, which lead to social, emotional and cognitive impairment, then to health risk behaviours like smoking weed, drugs, cigarettes and teen pregnancy, then to disease, disability, social problems and early death. Then you raise your children in the same environment. That is why so many of our fathers, mothers and grandparents never left the hood: they were products of their environment, with no knowledge. They know that if they put you in the worst condition possible, you will die early.

We are fighting against Satan, and Satan has an agenda to destroy the children of Israel; his people who get caught up in it are collateral damage. Look at the categories: emotional, physical and sexual abuse; emotional and physical neglect. Most of our community is on the chart three times off the bat. They go hand in hand: a child who was abused was also neglected, with no one watching out for her. Feeding children processed food, sugar and corn syrup and not making them exercise is physical neglect. Tuning your children out and giving them an iPad instead of time is emotional neglect, and it leads them to be sick as adults; that is why TikTok and the shorts are destroying our children from a young age. Then household dysfunction: domestic violence, substance abuse, mental illness, separation and divorce, crime. A brother who had to raise a mentally ill brother while his mother worked two jobs grew up resentful and selfish. Someone who falls into every category dies at 36, 40, 51, and they say gone too soon, while Esau sits back saying, exactly where I wanted him.

The risk factors follow: alcoholism, smoking, drug use, obesity, suicide attempts, depression, anxiety, teen pregnancy, miscarriage, domestic violence, a poor quality of life. Obesity is not something you just become; it is something you learned, from the way you grew up, and you can reset it. Many miscarriages among our sisters stem from trauma in the mind and stress in the body; you have to believe the word of God, forgive and let it go. Then the diseases: lung and heart disease, liver disease, sexually transmitted diseases from having sex early outside of marriage, lung cancer from cigarettes and weed, and death before 65. They know this. That is why they take crafty counsel against God’s people.

“They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” That decay is our degeneracy, and this is our mission: we have to restore the decayed state of our people and fight for our people. That is why we have to learn this terminology, learn the word of God, apply it to our life, and go out and teach our people.

A child who does not learn trust carries suspicion of the world into adulthood; a child not affirmed grows into an adult plagued by insecurity; a young person with no stable identity spends decades looking for himself in relationships, achievements or addictions. This is our life, and they have known it. They said, do not teach this to them; keep them in these conditions, degenerate.

Childhood trauma is not merely a past event: when the steps of development are missed, the wound is carried forward into how we think, how we love and who we are in the spirit. Healing has to go back to where the wound took place. That means I have to forgive my father, forgive my mother, and let it go, because holding on to it is affecting my mental and physical health. God designed children to receive guidance through their parents, grounded in his law. When parents are absent, wounded or disengaged, we open up portals to Satan.

precepts.why: “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord planted us a noble vine: he gave us the commandments and the scriptures and made us the elite, the top people on the planet, holy and right. “How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Lord looked at us and said, how did you become degenerate?

How did we become that degenerate plant? Verse 19 tells it: “Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee”. That is how we became degenerate: our own wickedness. “Know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.” Look at our conditions. We are feeling it now.

sense.text:
Born into a curse: the curse of Deuteronomy 28 is a pattern of traumatic, oppressive conditions handed down generation to generation, fatherlessness, abuse, poverty, broken covenant. These are not accidents. They are the fruit of curses left unbroken. That is us.

Read Deuteronomy 28 and you see trauma, trauma, trauma. “And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”. A trembling heart is trauma, a wounded heart. Sorrow of mind is constant depression and anxiety.

It is code switching: at work I have to be a certain way, and when I get home I have to shut it off, because my wife and children feel what I endure on the job and in the world every day as a black man. I have to decompress before I walk through the door. You can’t even talk to another black man on the job about the truth; he’ll tell the boss you are holding Bible study at six in the morning.

“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Your heart drops when your boss calls. No man should have that power over your life. You hush your wife and children to answer, not knowing if he will call you back in or complain. Months after leaving a job you can still feel that work phone vibrating in your pocket.

“In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” In the morning you can’t wait for the work day to be over; then you get home to the noise and can’t wait for the sun to come up. That is us. “For the fear of thine heart wherewith thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.”

Greenleaf shows it: a family whose son was killed by evil men in North Carolina moved west in the great migration for a better life, moved into a white neighbourhood and was terrorized. A daughter, through her trauma, got pregnant and had twins; the twins were given up to foster care, abused, separated, and the boy became a serial killer. That is intergenerational trauma: the psychological and physical effects of trauma passed from one generation to the next. War, oppression and abuse change a family’s environment, behaviour and even how genes are expressed, leaving the children more prone to anxiety, depression and PTSD. You feel a certain way and don’t know why: you feel your father’s pain.

Epigenetics: traumatic experiences can cause chemical changes that affect how genes are expressed, leaving the children with a lower baseline for handling stress. “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”. That is intergenerational trauma. You pass those conditions down to the next generation, who pass it down to the next, unless something breaks it. And that something is repentance and knowledge as an Israelite.

precepts.why:
“And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth. And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?” Why would the disciples ask that? Because they understood epigenetics and intergenerational trauma; they understood Deuteronomy 28. These were not dumb carpenters and fishermen walking around in the desert. These men had the wisdom of God; they were psychologists.

That should light a fire under you: your forefathers were the greatest men on earth and we descend from them. There is nothing we can’t do and no knowledge we can’t learn. If you didn’t graduate high school, get your GED, go to college, get a degree. Once we learn it, it’s a wrap.

sense.text: “What mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge?” The present generation was punished for what their forefathers did, especially in the days of Manasseh, and the people were quick to plead their own innocence however great their crimes. They used the proverb to say: I am this way because my father was this way.

“As I live, saith the Lord God, ye shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.” The Lord is saying: I am not letting you use the fact that you went through intergenerational trauma, or that your fathers were not right.

“Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” From here on, the soul that sins dies. You are not going to say, my daddy was wicked, so I’ll be wicked by default. You are going to change it.

“Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like”: a son who sees his father’s sins, considers them, and does not do the same.

“When the son hath done that which is lawful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son”.

Yes, intergenerational trauma is real. But do you sit in it, or do you change? This son changed, and he will not die though his father will. Just because our fathers were wicked and our mothers did not know God’s laws and taught us evil, that is not an excuse to stay in it. Recognize it and move on from it. “The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.”

precepts.why:
“Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

Although we have been through trauma, the Lord says he will still have mercy. He came to call sinners to repentance, and that is every last one of us. So we cannot use the excuse of what we have been through anymore. Christ has given us a clean slate.

sense.text:
The brain’s reward system releases dopamine when we do things that feel good, so we want to repeat them. That is why people get addicted to sex, drugs and overeating. We should get our dopamine from the fellowship and the work of the ministry. When you first come into the truth you are excited, then you go numb and fall back into old ways. You have to change it.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. Because we grew up in a world of sin, our pleasures are in sin; our dopamine comes from doing wicked things against God. But you can change the brain. The brain is not static: it can form new ideas and change habits, and you control it.

“What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” The only way you know you are in sin is by going back to God’s laws. You read that he said don’t do this, and you change it. Love me, keep the commandments: so I have to learn to love God’s commandments, fellowship, be around my family, build myself up, fast and pray, stop watching porn, stop smoking weed, stop being argumentative and contentious with my husband. You learn it through God’s laws. That is how you get the brain right.

“But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.” Concupiscence is an intense, often sensual longing or desire; in Christian teaching, the disordered human inclination to sin, from selfish, worldly or carnal appetites. That is the sinful nature, the shapen in iniquity: the inclination to sin. And we can change it.

precepts.why:
An example of concupiscence. “Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed”. A hot mind is a lustful mind. “A fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he hath kindled a fire.” That is the inclination to sin.

“All bread is sweet to a whoremonger”: that is the dopamine he has to have. Brothers in the world stayed in the club till the lights came on, not to have a good time but to see who the stragglers were. A sister still there when the lights came on was easy: she was looking for something, and would go home with anybody that night. And the whoremonger with prospects texted one prospect after another until somebody said yes. That is the whoremonger’s conversation; it is spoken from experience. Horrible. That is the inclination to sin.

“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.” You get hardened because you have been in sin so long you start to think it is the only way. No: God’s laws are the way.

sense.text: Trauma researchers found that the nervous system stores unresolved traumatic experiences and reactivates them in response to cues in the environment. That is why the Bible says: “If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding.”

precepts.why:
“The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.” You cannot sit among the people who put you through all these traumatic experiences, or who remind you of the time you turned to drugs, sex and alcohol. Separate yourself from them, and be around like-minded people on the same healing journey.

Some love their mama so much they will sit in her house and hear her speak evil of what they believe, of their husband, their lifestyle and how they raise their kids, and just take it, not knowing it is triggering the old trauma. You suppress the gospel around her and trim your ways to seek love, because around her, your uncle or your grandparents you feel like that little boy again who couldn’t say anything. If you don’t have the courage to tell your mother, I am keeping the commandments, and if you don’t like it you won’t see your grandkids, then don’t go to her house. If family will not respect your beliefs, stay away from them. Otherwise you are bringing yourself back to that old place and hindering your walk in this truth. Many men who are not growing in the spirit are still holding on to past crap.

sense.text: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.”

Neuroplasticity is the brain’s lifelong ability to reorganize itself, forming new connections and rewiring old ones through learning and repeated behaviour. The brain is not hardwired; it can be rewired through intentional, consistent thought. So if you say, I am going to keep God’s commandments, you can retrain your mind and body to keep God’s laws. Don’t let your traumatic experiences keep shaping who you are; your identity was formed in a false self. Let it go.

Before there was ever a word neuroplasticity, before Esau came up with these terms, Paul had the wisdom from Christ: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” Who is going to tell you that you can’t change when God says you can? You are an Israelite of Judah, Benjamin, Levi. God gave you the commandments and sent his Son to die for you. His grace is sufficient.

The brain can heal, but you have to put it through rigorous training: I’m not watching that, not eating that, not smoking or drinking that, not sleeping with her or him, I’m keeping myself chaste, I’m off the phone after a certain time, I’m deleting my Instagram. Stop saying you can’t lose weight or can’t stop having sex. You can, thus saith the Lord. Esau knows you can change; that is why he tells black people and our children they can’t, that science, law and medicine are for white people. No, that is for the Israelites, because our forefathers were psychologists before the white man came up with the term.

precepts.why:
Repentance is one of the ways to rewire your brain. “That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man”. If you believe this truth, God will strengthen your mind and give you the power to overcome your lust. If you fall into lust, your belief is not there yet; you have to fight it within, in the inner man.

“That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.” That deletes depression and anxiety. I don’t sit around depressed anymore: I know who orders my steps, what God called me to do, and that my brothers love me. If they get on me when I make a mistake, it is not from malice. But if you think everybody is evil because of what you went through, and you have not rewired your mind to see these as men of God and leaders, every correction will throw you back into the same rut and the same excuses.

Since the white man wants a big word, here is neuroplasticity in the Bible: “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts; And be renewed in the spirit of your mind”. Our forefathers told you over 1,900 years ago that you can change your mind. “And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

How do you rewire the brain? “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.” Catch yourself when you are about to lie. This is my neighbour and I love him, so I will tell him the truth, even admit that I was wrong. “Be ye angry, and sin not”: it is all right to be angry, but don’t let it make you fall into sin. “Let not the sun go down upon your wrath”: don’t lose the wisdom God gave you.

“Neither give place to the devil.” That is trauma. Satan can only use what is within you; deal with it and he can’t use it. But he uses the old thoughts: see how they treat you, they never liked you. And you agree with Satan. When we paid your rent, helped with your car, kept your kids a week while your wife was in the hospital and brought her food, was that hate? No. It is the same old trauma you keep returning to. The Lord said forgive. Let it go.

sense.text:
Another way to rewire the brain is meditation. “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” We think it is talking about money. No: you are going to change your mind and live a better life.

We are putting our kids through the same adverse experiences we went through and expecting them to change. We have to show them what change looks like, so that if all of us die, the generation behind us has the tools of repentance and does not fall into the trauma we went through. We protect our daughters from rape and our sons from molestation. We are a family. So meditate on the laws day and night.

precepts.why: “My hands also will I lift up unto thy commandments, which I have loved; and I will meditate in thy statutes.” Where is the meditation? In the statutes.
“Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.”

“Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” Your mind must be stayed on the Lord. Why would you have peace? Because you trust in the Lord. That is why your mind is at peace.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. “To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing”. What is the refreshing? Precept upon precept.

David said it, Isaiah said it, Sirach said it, Joshua said it. By today’s definition these men were psychologists, therapists and counsellors, and they knew how to heal their people. We must develop the same skill: find out what makes our people tick and help them heal from it.

“For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things.” What heals all things? The word of the Lord. We have been taking medication, being sedated, smoking weed and taking antidepressants, and the whole time the key to breaking ourselves from this trauma has been the Bible, the laws of God.

The most High put it on the spirit of Bishop Nathanyel to see it in the scriptures and bring it to the other bishops: keep the laws with the faith in Christ. The bishops and deacons have taught the captains, the captains teach the officers, the officers the soldiers, the soldiers the men, and the men their wives and children, and we take our kingdom back. That has been the solution the whole time. There is no other way: it is the word of God. You must meditate in God’s law, love this Bible, and use it as your medicine.

sense.text: “Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel.” Don’t give your mind over to heaviness, and stop overthinking. Deacon Labachaa said it long ago: self, shut the hell up. We laugh, but it is psychological. When you talk to yourself, it comes from a place of trauma: you are convincing yourself that the way you have been living is okay. You have to convince yourself it is not okay, that you are wrong and God is right. It is the word of God you are supposed to give heed to.
“The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days.” When you are joyful, you prolong your days.

“Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many, and there is no profit therein.” Love yourself; remove sorrow and grief from you. How many people die of depression and sorrow? Sirach was speaking as a doctor would today.

The study of how the mind, nervous system and immune system work together has shown that chronic stress and grief weaken the immune system: the killer cells that fight illness decrease and inflammation rises, bringing pain, fatigue and infection. That is why some get physically sick after losing a loved one. Their body is not weak; it is overwhelmed, taxed by the emotional weight it carries. Science knows this, and yet they push things into our community to keep us in this condition and mindset.

A psychosomatic illness is a real physical condition caused or made worse by chronic stress, anxiety or trauma. It is not imaginary; the brain and body are one, connected through the nervous system. If you are not in the right mind, not right with the Lord, it affects your physical condition. Sirach told us this in ancient times; we just have the terminology now.

precepts.why:
“Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” When someone passes, we are supposed to weep and moan, especially for those among us who are worthy. But he gives a time: a day or two, lest people call you wicked for not mourning. Then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Of grief comes death: that is the psychosomatic illness. The heavy heart is wounded. “Take no heaviness to heart: drive it away”. Don’t take heaviness to heart, brothers and sisters. “Forget it not, for there is no turning again: thou shalt not do him good, but hurt thyself.” You won’t do the one who died any good; you only hurt yourself.

Many of our illnesses are self-inflicted because we do not believe God’s word and do not let it work in our life, so we fall into the same trap over and over.

sense.text: Repentance, meditation, and now faith. “But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.” You must diligently seek him and believe that he is: that he can heal you from your past and from your trauma.

precepts.why: Christ told the apostles to forgive, even seventy times seven, and they answered: “Increase our faith.” If we are going to let go of all that, we need the Lord to increase our faith. That should be our prayer: that the Lord increase our faith to get us past these roadblocks.
How does he increase our faith? “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” That is how you build your faith.

sense.text: Repentance, meditation in God’s word, faith in God’s word, and fasting, cleaning your body up. “Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.” That is the only way to get rid of certain demons. You have to believe his word, meditate in it, change your mind according to it, and then fast.

Fellowship. People say, they can’t help me. You underestimate the power of unity. “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” For real healing you need brothers around you, people you trust, and the prayer of the righteous. “The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.” You need a body of believers around you, so you will not sit among those who plagued you in times past.

precepts.why: “Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.” If you believe God is in these men and women, you will fellowship, and that will help you heal from your trauma and the things you have been through.

“And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works”. When you come around the body you get provoked to love and good works. You have no time to sit back and sulk and pine away; you have brothers and sisters exhorting you.

“Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another”. Stop missing the Sabbath, the new moon, the study circle, the Friday night fellowship. Get your ass to the fellowship so you can get over the crap in your spirit, and be sincere about your healing journey, because many of us have not yet healed.

“And so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.” There is a day we will have to lay our life down for the Son of God. If you cannot be among your brothers and build with them, you will not stand in that day. You will give up and leave, because you have no foundation.

sense.text: Our nervous systems are corruptible, but the Lord is going to change this nervous system and this body. “And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Back to what was read at the start: we will bear the image of the heavenly.
“Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption.” What we are in now is corruption.

“Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.” No more trauma, no more weak nervous system constantly breaking down. The Lord says: you have earned it; I am taking you out of that corruptible body. “For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.”

precepts.why:
This is our reward. “For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body”. He is going to change this vile, corruptible body and fashion us like him; we will look and feel and be like him.

“According to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.” His power is so great that he will give us a piece of it. As he subdues all things, he will say, go out and subdue these nations, and your mind will just say yes sir. No more thought of what they did to me in my corruptible flesh. That mind is gone.

Christ and the angels do not hold on to traumatic experiences; they don’t have the nervous system we have. “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. That is immortality. When the Lord gives us immortality we will never second-guess him again. He puts his laws in your mind and you are programmed to move as God commands; no second-guessing, no free will. That is what Christ and the angels have in their mind: God’s laws. The power has been in God’s laws the whole time.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.”

“For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean”. The clean water is the commandments of God: he will put his laws in our mind and give us that immortal body. No more sin, no more nervous system to make you feel bad, no more of these somatic sicknesses, mental and physical issues and trauma. The Lord says, I am taking all that and cleaning you up: “from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.”

“A new heart also will I give you”: a new mind, a new body, a new nervous system. “And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh”: the sinful heart. At the start of the class we read that Adam had a wicked heart; the Lord says, I will remove that. “And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them. And ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

“In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded. And the desolate land shall be tilled”. First he changes us; then he changes the land to conform to us. The world was made for us, but he cannot give us Jerusalem as it is supposed to be while we are in the midst of sin. He cleanses us, gives us a new heart, removes this weak, brittle body and gives us immortality, and then commands the land to transform: “This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. We go right back to where we were in the beginning with our father Adam, and we will be with our father again, Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah.

“Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.”
